title: Quasi-coherent affine candidate from torsion-controlled formal gluing
statement: Let X be affine Noetherian, J ideal sheaf data, H coherent, N a coherent formal module, and delta:N -> completion(H). Assume a single positive power of J annihilates the kernels and cokernels of every component of delta [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. There exist a quasi-coherent X-module F, a map a:F -> H, and an isomorphism beta:N.obj -> formalCompletionFunctor(J)(F), factoring delta through completion(a). One positive power of J annihilates both kernel(a) and cokernel(a). No coherence or finite generation of F is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0889(1), affine construction, using Tags 087W, 0888, 00MA and 0ALK(1)

proof.text: Identify the affine scheme with Spec A via its canonical isomorphism. Use the affine formal-module equivalence to represent N by a finite completed module Q and the coherent H by a finite A-module P. The natural completion tensor comparison identifies the map with Q -> S tensor P, where S is the I-adic completion. Transfer the componentwise bound to a positive annihilating power for its kernel and cokernel; the exponent may change.

The completion ring map is flat and has the same quotient modulo I. Formal gluing 0ALK(1) provides an A-module T, a map T -> P and Q isomorphic to S tensor T, with the required factorization. Its comparison isomorphisms identify the kernel and cokernel with those of Q -> S tensor P as A-modules. Transfer the positive uniform annihilating power through these linear equivalences. No finite generation of T is asserted.

Sheafify T and its map; tilde is quasi-coherent and exact. The affine ideal-product and kernel/cokernel formulas transfer the uniform bound to sheaves. For every positive n, A/I^n -> S/I^n S is an isomorphism (apply the completion quotient comparison to I^n, or iterate the I-adic quotient comparison). Right exactness of tensor identifies T/I^n T with (S tensor T)/I^n(S tensor T), even for arbitrary T. Compose these identifications with Q and the affine formal equivalence reconstruction to produce beta. Naturality makes its components compatible with reduction and proves the factorization. This avoids using completion-as-tensor for the possibly infinite T.

For I=A, the coherent formal system is zero; choose T=P, the identity map and the unique isomorphism of zero quotient systems. For I=0, the constant formal system is its own limit; the affine equivalence gives the original map and T=Q. The zero ring or empty spectrum has the same construction.

mathlib_searches.query: Formal gluing constructs a quasi coherent module on a Noetherian affine scheme with prescribed completed quotient system and a map whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by an ideal power
A finite completed module mapping to the completion of a finite module with ideal power torsion kernel and cokernel algebraizes over a Noetherian affine scheme

lean.statement:
theorem torsionControlled_affine_candidate
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsAffine X] (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (H : CoherentModules X) (N : CoherentFormalModule X J)
    (δ : N ⟶ (completion X J).obj H)
    (htorsion : ∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧ ∀ e : ℕ,
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι t).2
        (kernel (δ.hom.app (op e)))) ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι t).2
        (cokernel (δ.hom.app (op e))))) :
    ∃ (F : X.Modules) (_ : F.IsQuasicoherent) (a : F ⟶ H.obj)
      (β : N.obj ≅ (formalCompletionFunctor J).obj F),
      δ.hom = β.hom ≫ (formalCompletionFunctor J).map a ∧
      (∃ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s ∧
        IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2
          (kernel a)) ∧
        IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2
          (cokernel a)))
